images.title: Worth of an offering on a balance
images.purpose: Shows Roxie balanced by an equal weight of jaggery, so the worth is 45 × 70 = 3150 rupees.
images.composition: Plain white background, lots of empty space around the main object, no scenery, no people, no extra text. One large two-pan balance in the centre with a simple figure on one pan and jaggery blocks on the other, and the calculation below.
images.exact_structure: A level two-pan balance drawn in dark outline with a grey (#6B7280) stand. Left pan: one simple flat teal (#0072B2) figure silhouette with no face details, labelled 'Roxie 45 kg' under the pan. Right pan: a neat stack of exactly 6 flat amber (#E69F00) jaggery blocks, labelled 'jaggery 45 kg' under the pan. Below the balance, the label '70 rupees per kg' and then '45 × 70 = 3150' in a reddish purple (#CC79A7) rounded box. The beam is exactly level. Exactly 1 figure, 6 blocks, 1 box.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: Worth = weight in kg × cost of 1 kg.
images.description: Shows Roxie balanced by an equal weight of jaggery, so the worth is 45 × 70 = 3150 rupees.
images.context: Assumed values: 45 kg and 70 rupees a kg give 3150 rupees; wheat for Estu: 50 × 50 = 2500 rupees.
images.teaching_notes: The 6 blocks only stand for the jaggery; they are not 6 kg each in any exact sense, so do not count them.

image_decisions.why: The balance makes the model worth = weight × cost per kg visible, which is the estimating idea of this concept.
